title: I direct, Claude writes the code: what I learned shipping a free Android arcade game. Feedback wanted
author: Fancy-Proof-9449
selftext:
Hi all. I released a game on Google Play this week and want to share how it was made, because almost none of the code was typed by me. (Links are in the first comment: my first try at this post had them in the body and got caught by the spam filter.)

**The game.** Afterimage is a free arcade game for Android. Everything you do is recorded and comes back as Replicas that replay your exact path a few seconds behind you. Touch one and the run is over, so the longer you last, the more of your own past you have to dodge. There are also levels, a Waves mode, a Hero Mode with classes, talents and bosses, and an online mode.

**How AI was used.** I'm a solo dev and I don't write the code by hand. I decide what the game should be, play every build on my phone and judge it. Claude (through Claude Code) designs, writes, reviews and tests the TypeScript. A few things I learned that may be useful here:

**Write down the rules that must never break.** They live in plain words in a file the AI reads at the start of every session. For this game that means things like "a Replica always stays behind the live player" and "the arena is the same size on every device". Without that file, a later change quietly undoes an earlier decision.

**Make it prove things, and don't trust a new check until you've seen it fail.** Every build runs about 35 automated checks (the simulation, map generation, purchases, even the wording of the text players read) and refuses to build if one fails. A check only counts once it has been shown failing against the old code.

**Feel can't be automated.** Joystick feel, difficulty and music took many rounds of me playing on a real phone and saying what was wrong. The AI is good at measuring things. It can't tell you whether something is fun or whether a sound is ugly.

**No art or sound files.** Every visual is drawn in code and every sound is synthesized, apart from a few voice lines I recorded myself. That kept the whole project in text, which is where an AI coding tool is strongest. The trailers are made the same way: a script cuts the footage on a beat grid and synthesizes the drum score.

**What I'd love from you.** Tell me what you like and what you dislike, especially in the first couple of minutes. Happy to answer anything about the workflow.
